How it works

A simple match. A lifelong impact.

  1. 1

    Apply

    Service members and volunteers create a profile and tell us about their situation, their animals, and their experience.

  2. 2

    Match

    Our team pairs each animal with a screened local volunteer based on species, needs, location, and lifestyle.

  3. 3

    Care

    Volunteers provide loving care and monthly photo updates while service members stay focused on the mission.

  4. 4

    Reunite

    When orders end, we bring pets home — and keep the connection between the family and their volunteer strong.

Our mission

No Animal Left Behind is a nonprofit dedicated to protecting the bond between service members and their animals. We provide free, vetted foster care during deployment so that a set of orders never becomes a surrender form.

Read our FAQ ›

  • Trusted

    Every volunteer is screened, referenced, and checked in on.

  • Compassionate

    We treat every animal like family, from day one to homecoming.

  • Community

    Neighbors stepping up for the people who step up for us.

Support the mission

$45 covers one month of food and vet reserve for one animal.

Donations cover veterinary emergencies, food stipends, transport to a volunteer's home, and the background checks that keep every match safe. Service members are never charged.

Demo only — no payment processor is connected and no money can be taken.

Other ways to help

  • Transport Drive an animal from a base to a volunteer's home.
  • Veterinary partners Offer discounted care in your area.
  • Supplies Send food, crates, or bedding from our wish list.
  • Spread the word Tell a unit family readiness group we exist.

Questions

Before you apply

Does this cost a service member anything?

No. Care is provided by volunteers at no cost. Our fund covers routine food stipends and emergency veterinary care when a family can't.

How far in advance should I apply?

As early as you have orders. Sixty days gives us the best chance of a nearby match, but we take urgent requests and work them first.

Who is eligible?

Active-duty, Guard, and Reserve members with deployment, TDY, or unaccompanied orders. We also help with training pipelines and medical hospitalization case by case.

How are volunteers screened?

Application, two references, a background check, a video home walkthrough, and a trial visit with the animal before any handoff.

What if the deployment gets extended?

Extensions are common and we plan for them. We confirm with your volunteer, and if they can't continue, we arrange a new match and cover transport.

What kinds of animals can you place?

Dogs and cats most often, plus birds, small mammals, reptiles, and occasionally horses where we have a specialist volunteer.

What paperwork is involved?

A care agreement signed by both parties, current vaccination records, a veterinary release, and an emergency contact who can act on your behalf.
